title: Formalized provability: reasoning about proofs inside arithmetic

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Express proof checking and consistency in arithmetic, and distinguish numerical proofs from the uniform derivability conditions.
abstract: An arithmetic formula can describe a finite proof, so arithmetic can also express the claim that a proof exists. Starting with the proof checker used for first incompleteness, we show how an actual proof supplies an arithmetic proof of its own provability. We then combine certified proofs by an explicit numerical operation and examine what arithmetic proves about each concrete calculation. This leads to a precise distinction: verifying every ordinary numerical instance does not by itself establish a statement about all the numbers in an arithmetic model. We formulate the stronger derivability conditions, check their truth in the standard model, and identify the additional internal proofs they demand. Finally we write the consistency sentence for our chosen predicate and establish exactly what it means in the standard model.
